target_customer: Satellite operators and spacecraft builders, including defense and aerospace, that need more power in orbit
problem: Spacecraft must generate all their own power, which caps what can be built and operated in orbit. Central Blue plans satellites that collect sunlight and beam power by laser to other spacecraft.
business_model: Power as a service sold to spacecraft operators, with hardware receivers and grid control software

founders.name: Brian Wu
education: Stanford, BS and MS in computer science
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page; also lists experience with autonomy startups for drones and space rovers.

founders.name: Jeewoo Choi
prior_employers: Boeing Defense, Space & Security (thermal, airflow and environmental testing)
education: Stanford, BS and MS in mechanical engineering

competitors.name: Star Catcher Industries
competitors.what: Space to space optical power beaming grid for satellites
competitors.traction_then: Reported a record optical power transmission test at Kennedy Space Center and planned an on-orbit demo in 2026
competitors.funding_then: $65M Series A in May 2026 on top of a $12.25M seed in July 2024, about $88M total per trade press

competitors.name: Mantis Space
competitors.what: Laser power beaming network for satellites in eclipse

technical_complexity.rationale: Space-grade laser power beaming between moving spacecraft needs precise pointing, thermal management and radiation-hardened hardware. A prototype is said to be nearly complete in Seattle, but nothing has flown.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware depth and space heritage are hard to copy, but better funded rivals (Star Catcher at $88M) are ahead on demos.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early at the Fall 2026 batch; rivals were funded and testing, none had bought or absorbed the wedge.

market_need_then: Satellites are limited by onboard power and eclipse periods, and trade press in 2026 showed investor appetite for orbital power grids (Star Catcher $65M Series A, Mantis $10M seed).

identity.visual_style: Dark, minimal, spacecraft renders and hardware photos
identity.voice_and_tone: Short bold headlines, tagline 'The Power Grid for Space'

brand_strength.rationale: New, with a clean but generic name and no press about the brand.

outcome_analysis: Central Blue is an active Fall 2026 company founded in 2026 by two Stanford engineers with NASA JPL and Boeing space backgrounds. No exit, shutdown or layoffs were found, and no funding round is documented. The outcome is open; the main risks are hardware difficulty and capital needs against better funded rivals.
notes: Dealroom (AI generated text, one aggregator) lists a $125k seed and describes the company as spacecraft servicing robotics in Palo Alto, which conflicts with YC and the company site; unverified and not recorded as a round. The company site says it is backed by Y Combinator but gives no amounts. Founders are not named on the company site; they come from the YC page.
